project_specification.project_name: nullius — feature 336 (System rejects a purge configuration for forward data, because the record is out of sample by construction)
project_specification.addition_summary:
Implement app_spec.xml feature 336 in the existing `forward` plugin (packages/forward, import name forward; seat src/app/modules/forward): the prohibition that enforces docs/alpha-engine-prd.md §5 Loop 3's own closing line — *"After 90 days, that signal has a track record on data that **did not exist when the hypothesis was formed**. No purging scheme is needed; the data is honestly out of sample by construction."* — read on its one operative clause this member has not yet enforced: a configuration whose intent is to purge forward-record data is **rejected**, because the record is out of sample by construction and is therefore never purgeable. docs/nullius-tech-architecture.md §13.4 states the same rule from the other side: *"After 90 days it has a record on data that did not exist when the hypothesis was formed, so no purging scheme is needed."*
Feature 335 built the fact this feature builds on: a forward observation is honest only while the window is open, and at the close the signal *has* its 90-day track record on data that did not exist when the hypothesis was formed. Feature 336 adds the prohibition that the record that 335 proves is out of sample by construction may not be purged. One act, one module: `purge.py` holds the record, the validator, the fact and the verdict. `ForwardPurgeConfig` is the purge configuration as the sentence's object: a frozen record of exactly two fields — `target` (the data scope the purge would remove, a non-empty string naming a table) and `cutoff_days` (the retention window — how many days of history the purge keeps, a positive integer) — and it is deliberately the operator's own document, not a re-derivation of the record: the configuration names its own target and carries its own window, and neither is inferred from the rows. `rejects_ forward_purge(config)` is the sentence's *rejects*: it validates the ask whole first (`ForwardPurgeConfigRequestError`, no code word — a malformed configuration names its target in its first words) and then **raises** `ForwardPurgeRejectedError` when the configuration names the forward record — the table feature 108's migration gave this member (`forward_record`) — returning None when the configuration names any other table. The refusal opens with the greppable code `forward_purge_rejected`, names the target and the window, cites §5 Loop 3 (*"No purging scheme is needed; the data is honestly out of sample by construction"*), and states the one repair that exists — the record is the only source of genuinely uncontaminated evidence, so it is kept, never purged. `is_forward_purge(config)` is the read-only spelling — the fact without the refusal — answering True exactly when a configuration names the forward record.
The boundary is the **target**, not the window. This member judges one thing — does the configuration name the forward record — and deliberately not the window's length: a `cutoff_days` of zero is not a *worse* purge of the record, it is a malformed window, and it is refused as the ask's own fact (`ForwardPurgeConfigRequestError`) before any judgment of the target is formed, so a caller that handed a broken window is told *state the window* rather than *the record may not be purged*. A `cutoff_days` of a thousand on a purge of the ledger is answered None — the window is irrelevant to a target this member does not judge — and a `cutoff_days` of one on a purge of the record is refused, because the target is the record and the record is out of sample by construction. The ask is total before the judgment: a present configuration that is not a well-stated `ForwardPurgeConfig` (a blank target, a non-string target, a non-positive or non-integer window) is refused as `ForwardPurgeConfigRequestError` before any target is judged, so a caller that handed a broken configuration is told *state the configuration*, never *the record may not be purged*.
No central registry, router, app factory, middleware, settings or migration is edited; the member joins by workspace-scan convention, adds no `@register`, no table and no endpoint, and imports no other workspace member — the configuration and the record arrive as records because a member never re-derives a fact it was handed. The module is stdlib-only at module scope (`dataclasses`, `typing` and the member's own `.errors`), so the factory's scan — which imports this package on every `create_app()` to fire its `@register` — pays nothing for the prohibition beyond the import it already paid for the record, the observation, the retention, the priors and the beta-four acts.

feature.description: System rejects a purge configuration for forward data, because the record is out of sample by construction. It exposes `ForwardPurgeConfig` — the purge configuration as the sentence's object — as a frozen record of exactly two fields: `target` (the data scope the purge would remove, a non-empty string naming a table) and `cutoff_days` (the retention window — how many days of history the purge keeps, a positive integer). Construction validates each field in declaration order and refuses with `ForwardPurgeConfigRequestError` what cannot be part of a stated configuration: a blank or non-string target, or a non-positive or non-integer window. The record is the operator's own document made structural — a purge that names no window cannot be judged — and it carries nothing else: the target is a free name (the table the purge would remove) and the window is a free count, and neither is re-derived from the rows.

System exposes `is_forward_purge(config)` — the read-only spelling of feature 336's prohibition. It validates the ask whole first (the configuration's two fields, `ForwardPurgeConfigRequestError`, before any target is judged — a present-but-broken configuration is refused as the ask's own fact, not judged against the record), and answers True exactly when a configuration names the member's own forward record (`forward_record`) and False when it names any other data scope. The shape `forward.retention` takes for its own fact: validate the ask, answer a fact, and let the caller decide what to do with it.

System exposes `rejects_forward_purge(config)` — the sentence's *rejects*. It reads the configuration's `target` / `cutoff_days` surface duck-typed (an absent attribute distinguished from a present-`None` one by sentinel, so the loader's synthetic-name copies are judged as well as canonical records), settles the configuration's ask whole in declaration order first (`ForwardPurgeConfigRequestError`, no code word, before any target is judged), and raises `ForwardPurgeRejectedError` when the configuration names the forward record, returning None when it names any other table. The refusal opens with `forward_purge_rejected`, names the target and the window, cites §5 Loop 3 (*"After 90 days, that signal has a track record on data that did not exist when the hypothesis was formed. No purging scheme is needed; the data is honestly out of sample by construction"*), and states the one repair that exists — the record is the only source of genuinely uncontaminated evidence, so it is kept, never purged. A refused configuration forms no value.

System defines the prohibition's two refusal classes in the member's one error module, as siblings under feature 332's `ForwardError` — the one-base-per-member shape the dreaming and regime members state, so a caller that refuses forward work wholesale writes one `except` while a caller that must react differently to *your configuration could not be stated* and *the record may not be purged* catches the specific siblings. `ForwardPurgeConfigRequestError` is the ask's face and carries no code word (a malformed configuration names its target in its first words, the `ForwardRecordError` precedent); it refuses the configuration's two fields' own facts before any target is judged. `ForwardPurgeRejectedError` is the judgment and opens every message with `forward_purge_rejected`; its repair is its own — the record is out of sample by construction, so it is kept, never purged — which is why it is its own class and not the base (whose repair is *fix the signals*) or the ask (whose repair is *state the configuration*). Both are subclasses of the base and neither of the other.

System keeps the prohibition a free function beside the record rather than a second component: `purge.py` is imported by the member's `__init__.py`, which widens its re-export (the record, the predicate, the verdict and the two error classes join features 332's, 333's, 337's, 338's, 339's and 340's names) and gains no `@register`. No new component is composed, `app.order` still carries exactly one `forward`, and the seat (src/app/modules/forward) is unchanged and still re-exports nothing — a caller that wants the prohibition reaches the member's own namespace, the discipline every seat in this workspace states. The module is stdlib-only at module scope (`dataclasses`, `typing` and the member's own `.errors`), so the factory's scan — which imports this package on every `create_app()` to fire its `@register` — pays nothing for the prohibition beyond the import it already paid. No shared order-sensitive surface is authored into — no registry, router, app factory, middleware or settings — and no data is created or removed, because the prohibition judges a configuration the caller hands it. The prohibition judges a configuration the caller hands it; it opens nothing, reads nothing, sweeps no state and removes nothing — the deployment's wiring delivers the configuration through the verdict, and this module enforces only that the record is never purged.

System passes the prohibition over the member's own fixtures: a well-stated `ForwardPurgeConfig` naming another table runs (the verdict answers None); a configuration naming `forward_record` is refused with `ForwardPurgeRejectedError` opening with `forward_purge_rejected` and naming the target and the window; a present-but-broken configuration (blank target, non-string target, non-positive window, non-integer window) is refused at the ask with `ForwardPurgeConfigRequestError` and no code word, and the ask settles before the judgment (a broken configuration naming the record meets the ask first); a duck-typed stand-in carrying the configuration's two attributes is judged identically to the member's own record (the loader's synthetic-copy trap); an absent attribute is distinguished from a present-`None` one by sentinel; both error classes are subclasses of `ForwardError` and neither of the other; the module is stdlib-only parsed from the AST, imports no other member, opens no store, reads no environment and consults no clock; no verb accepts a window-length or content parameter (pinned through `inspect.signature`); and a re-run over the same configuration answers the identical verdict.
